predecessors.name: Taifa of Zaragoza
predecessors.text: Lérida, taken from the Banu Tujib wālīs in 1039 together with Zaragoza by al-Musta'in of the Banu Hud and given to a younger son

successors.name: Almoravid dynasty
successors.text: Lérida, which 'appears to have fallen to the Almoravids' in 1102 (others: 1110)

rulers.name: Yusuf al-Muzaffar ibn Sulayman ibn Hud

ledger.x: c. 1040: Lérida becomes a separate taifa under Yusuf, a son of al-Musta'in of the Banu Hud. 'Between c. 1040 and c. 1105, the Taifa of Lérida was separate from that of Zaragoza.' The Lleida page: taken from the Banu Tujib with Zaragoza in 1039; ruler Yusuf from 1039/1046; in 1046 'the elder son, Aḥmad al-Muḳtadir…
1078: civil war between the brothers Yusuf of Lérida and al-Muqtadir of Zaragoza, which 'reunited' the Hudid principality under al-Muqtadir by 1081 (page paraphrase: 1078-81).
1081: the civil war ends with al-Muqtadir master of the whole principality; 'When al-Muḳtadir died in late 1081, the ṭāʾifa was divided between his two sons.'
late 1081: al-Mundhir inherits Lérida at the division of al-Muqtadir's realm: 'The younger, al-Mundhir, who was already governing Denia and Tortosa as his father's ḥājib, inherited Lérida also.'
1081: al-Mundhir holds Tortosa with Lérida (a governorship, drawn as the dependent tint).
1081: al-Mundhir holds Denia with Lérida; the page has al-Muqtadir acquire Denia in 1076 and Tortosa in 1061.
1083: Graus falls: 'In 1083, they took Graus' (the passage does not name 'they'; read as the Aragonese, since Peter of Aragon takes the next towns).
1090: al-Mundhir dies and his minor son Sulayman succeeds; 'Sulaymān's regents divided the ṭāʾifa, separating Denia and Tortosa to their own advantage and leaving him a rump Lérida.'
1090: Denia separated from Lérida by Sulayman's regents (see Tortosa).
by 1093: 'between 1087 and 1093, Peter took Estada, Monzón and Almenar' (Peter, 'now king of Aragon' by 1100); dated at the end of the span.
1100: 'Peter, now king of Aragon, captured Barbastro, the second city of the ṭāʾifa, and Sariñena.'
1101: 'the capture of Pomar de Cinca and Albalate de Cinca brought the Aragonese up to Lérida itself.'
1102: Lérida 'appears to have fallen to the Almoravids that year, although others have it lasting until 1110'; the Zaragoza page has the separation end c.
1102: the Taifa of Lérida ends; the Almoravids 'appointed wālīs to govern it until it was captured by the Catalans in 1149'.

wars.name: Hudid civil war of 1078-1081
wars.outcome: The brothers' war reunited the Hudid principality under al-Muqtadir; on his death in late 1081 it was divided again and al-Mundhir took Lérida.

wars.name: Aragonese conquest of the Cinca valley and Barbastro
wars.outcome: The Aragonese took the taifa's northern and eastern towns one by one and reached Lérida by 1101; Ermengol IV of Urgell attacked toward Balaguer in 1089, 'possibly taking it briefly'.

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of Lérida
wars.outcome: Lérida fell to the Almoravids in 1102 (others: 1110) after Ermengol V of Urgell's defeat at Mollerussa.

certainty.note: The pages name towns and no boundaries; the extent is a reading of the later conquests.
